sources.entry: Lumilo - Open-source menu bar app that runs Splash or llama.cpp servers, shows memory and token speed, and downloads models from Hugging Face. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kotuke/lumilo) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Lumilo is an unofficial, open-source macOS menu-bar app that starts and stops local LLM servers (Splash or llama.cpp), shows memory and speed, downloads Hugging Face models, and launches coding agents against the server.
summary.what_it_does: Lumilo runs the Splash or llama.cpp (llama-server) engine as a child process, starting, stopping and restarting it and showing whether it is loading, ready, generating, unloaded or failed. The panel and menu-bar icon show memory against the engine's budget, tokens per second, time to first token, and a chart of the last 20 requests. Models can be searched on Hugging Face by name, sized and checked against available memory, downloaded beside a running server, queued, paused and resumed, or deleted with a note of how much space is freed. It can open Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Pi in Terminal, Ghostty or Rex already pointed at the local server. It also installs and updates the engine through Homebrew, and its settings cover port, network access, an API key stored in the Keychain, and idle unload.
use_cases: run a local LLM server on a Mac without using the terminal
monitor memory and token speed of a local model
download GGUF or MLX models from Hugging Face
point a coding agent at a local model server
manage and delete downloaded LLM models to free disk space
install and update llama.cpp or Splash via Homebrew
how_to_run: Open Lumilo from Applications; its icon appears in the menu bar
If no engine is installed, the panel offers to install it with Homebrew
Build: go tool mygo build (outputs build/darwin-arm64/Lumilo.app)
notable: Engines are pluggable through a documented Engine and Installer contract; mlx-serve is named as planned
Model downloads run apart from the server, with a queue, pause and resume that survive quitting the app
Server listens only on this Mac by default; network access requires an API key kept in the Keychain
Eight interface languages, including right-to-left Arabic layout
Signed with Developer ID and notarized, per the README
caveats: Requires macOS on Apple silicon; Splash itself needs macOS 26.4 or later
Needs Homebrew to install the engine
Unofficial, independent project not affiliated with Splash or other engines
Some translations (Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Spanish) were not reviewed by native speakers
